title: Mezzrow's European tour and the Sinatra tour of Italy
summary: Moore describes touring Europe with Mezz Mezzrow and then Frank Sinatra's Italian tour with Italian musicians.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Okay. Although you were with Lester Lanin for a while, you also went back to France in 1953, where you played with Francois Moustache Galapadis.

Let's see, I'm trying to recall what -- this was long before I went with Lanin. Things are going so fast right now. I did go back right after -- Oh, yes, I came back from the Festival of Jazz in Paris and I was invited by Mezz Mezzrow along with Red Richards, Kansas Fields, Gene Sedric, Buck Clayton -- all of us got a contract to go back to Paris for a tour in Europe. It was Mezz Mezzrow's project and we rehearsed and we played many of the principal cities and Paris and then we went to . . .

Okay, you went to North Africa and you were contracted to do what?

We were contracted to join Frank Sinatra on his tour of the principal cities in Italy, like Rome and Naples. At that time he was still married to Ava Gardner and so the band was augmented with Italian musicians who didn't speak a word of English and none of us could speak a word of Italian. So we had interpreters with the group and of course Frank paid for everything, you know. This one incident I remember very correctly, at the theater in Naples, according to the Italian version, Ava Gardner was advertised to appear at the theater and it wasn't right and Frank was right in getting angry. It didn't go with Frank Sinatra/very good to have his wife advertising to appear. What happened, I think it was something to draw the people in, that was the main thing. Frank wouldn't go on stage, he wouldn't do the show until they'd do something about that advertisement thing, that he got his papers. So remember the Italian contingent of the band -- they got into the hassle with the owners of the theater and even so far as to almost end up in fisticuffs. These Italians are very spirited, you know.

the first trombone player was Italian, and they were good readers, good musicians. I never dreamed that those Italians could be great musicians; sight readers--- even jazz; there were some guys there that played like Charlie Parker. They are not known yet. Anyway, the first trumpet player got in a hassle, he got in jail and Frank Sinatra went over and bailed him out and finally the tour that the shows were put on for the guy....there was an apology or something of that sort, and finally the tour got under way, we went to Rome, Bologna, all the principal cities.
